Section B: questions 32–41 carry 2 marks (30–50 words), questions 42–45 carry 3 marks (50–80 words) and questions 46–47 carry 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Home Science teaches both the art and the science of managing a home. (ii) Home Science is only for girls. (iii) A person who owns and finances an enterprise is self-employed. (iv) The school course in Home Science is enough to get a specialised job.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – it is for both boys and girls. (iii) True. (iv) False – it gives only basic knowledge; advanced courses are needed.

questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – there is no vaccine or cure.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name two self-employment opportunities for the youth in interior decoration.
questions.answer: Working as an interior designer, furniture designer, showroom or shop owner, show-case and window display designer, running a home-based craft centre or conducting hobby courses (any two).

questions.q: Write two differences between boiling and pressure cooking methods.
questions.answer: Boiling is done at 100 degrees C in an open pan with plenty of water and takes longer; pressure cooking is done above 100 degrees C in steam under pressure, takes about one-third of the time, saves fuel and needs little water. Pressure cooking kills all bacteria and loses less water-soluble vitamins.

questions.q: What does food preservation mean? Why is it important?
questions.answer: Preservation is a process by which food is prevented from spoiling for a short or long time while its colour, taste and nutritive value are kept as far as possible. It takes care of excess produce, adds variety, sends food to places where it is not grown and makes storage and transport easier.

questions.q: Give any four suggestions for safe garbage disposal in your area.
questions.answer: Collect garbage in a covered bin; dump in covered pits outside the city; use sanitary landfills; compost garden waste; incinerate in a furnace; never burn it in the open or throw it into water.

questions.q: What is meant by incubation period? Give one example.
questions.answer: It is the gap between the entry of germs and the appearance of the symptoms of the disease. For example, typhoid symptoms may appear 14–21 days after the infected food was eaten; the person is a carrier meanwhile.

questions.q: Distinguish between washing and dry cleaning.
questions.answer: Washing removes dirt with soap or detergent and water and suits colourfast fabrics; dry cleaning removes dirt with grease absorbents and solvents and is used for leather, fur, selected silks and woollens, zari and costly fabrics.

questions.q: Classify finishes on the basis of their functions and give two examples of each.
questions.answer: Basic (aesthetic) finishes – scouring, bleaching, starching, calendering, applied to almost all fabrics. Functional (special) finishes – fire-proof and waterproof, bullet-proof and crease-resistant finishes for a specific purpose.

questions.q: Explain 'peer' and give two positive effects of positive peer pressure.
questions.answer: A peer is a person of equal age, abilities, qualifications, background or social status. Positive peer pressure helps social development and self-esteem, gives a safety net in difficult times, provides role models and encourages healthy behaviour such as sports.

questions.q: What can be the four consequences of not following values in the society?
questions.answer: Loss of life and damage to public property; crime and corruption; breakdown of families and loss of law and order; alcohol and drug abuse; abuse of women, children and vulnerable people; wastage of resources.

questions.q: How can the cloth merchant cheat in measuring? Name any four signs.
questions.answer: Using a table to measure, a bent measuring rod, stretching the fabric while measuring, and selling cheap fabric at the price of a better one.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Your mother is cooking chapatti, dal and vegetables for lunch. Give one suggestion each to enhance the nutritive value of each dish.
questions.answer: Chapatti: mix pulses or soya flour or add grated vegetables (missi roti, methi paratha) to improve proteins and vitamins. Dal: add spinach, moong or other vegetables, or combine with rice (khichri), and cook in a covered pan without soda. Vegetable: cut into large pieces just before cooking, cook in a covered pan with little water and use the water.

questions.q: Write any six reasons for the increase in life style diseases.
questions.answer: (1) Fast food and junk food replacing nutritious balanced meals. (2) More processed and packed food, rich in sugar, fat and salt. (3) Soft drinks replacing milk. (4) Use of bus or car even for short distances. (5) Machines reducing physical labour. (6) Smoking and drinking among young people. (7) Stress. (8) Overweight and obesity.

questions.q: Analyse any six possible mistakes families make while selecting a bedroom.
questions.answer: Choosing a room that is noisy or lacks privacy; badly lit or poorly ventilated; too small or odd-shaped to place beds and furniture; far from the bathroom; near the kitchen or the entrance; ignoring storage; too much furniture; not considering that one-third of life is spent sleeping.

questions.q: Write any four points on the care of a newborn baby's cord and skin, and two on immunisation.
questions.answer: Wipe the baby with a clean cloth in warm water and do not scrub, because the white coating and fine hair are protective; keep the cut cord dry and open to air and cover it lightly only if there are flies and dust. Immunise on time: BCG and oral polio at birth, DPT at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, MMR at 9–12 months; it is free at government hospitals and health centres.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Reena spoiled her white cotton clothes while removing stains. What could be five possible reasons?
questions.answer: She may not have identified the stain and used the wrong agent; used a strong reagent that damaged the fabric; used heat on a protein stain so it set; let the stain become old before treating it; did not rinse the chemical out properly; or ironed before the stain was removed.

questions.q: Explain the steps in making a time plan and how dovetailing helps to save time.
questions.answer: Steps: list all the activities; group them as flexible (shopping) and inflexible (school, classes); estimate the time for each; balance the time by reducing time on some activities so the total fits within 24 hours. A good plan is practical and flexible, has an alternative for emergencies and allows rest and leisure. Dovetailing means doing two or three activities together: cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes take 80 minutes separately but only 55 minutes when dovetailed (starting the washing machine, boiling dal, cutting vegetables meanwhile), saving 25 minutes.
